landmarks.name: Home Island
landmarks.writeup: One of the two inhabited islands, known for its traditional Cocos Malay community and cultural heritage.

wiki.extract: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands, officially the Territory of Cocos (Keeling) Islands, are an Australian external territory located in the Indian Ocean, comprising a small archipelago approximately midway between Australia and Sri Lanka and relatively close to the Indonesian island of Sumatra. The territory's dual name reflects that the islands have historically been known as either the Cocos Islands or the Keeling Islands, the latter of which is still a common short name.

landmarks.name: Direction Island
landmarks.writeup: Famous for its natural beauty, coral reefs, and as a popular spot for snorkeling and diving.

wiki.extract: West Island, part of the South Keeling Islands, is the capital of the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, an Australian external territory in the Indian Ocean. The population is roughly 120, making it the third smallest capital in the world, and consists mainly of Europeans. It is less populous than Home Island, the only other inhabited island.

landmarks.name: West Island
landmarks.writeup: The administrative center of the territory, hosting government offices and the airport.

cultural_events.name: Hari Raya Aidilfitri
cultural_events.writeup: A significant Muslim festival celebrated by the Cocos Malay community marking the end of Ramadan.

wiki.extract: Eid al-Fitr is the first of the two main festivals in Islam, the other being Eid al-Adha. The holiday falls on the first day of Shawwal, the tenth month of the Islamic calendar. One of the most important Islamic celebrations, Eid al-Fitr is celebrated by Muslims worldwide as it marks the end of the month-long, dawn-to-dusk fasting (sawm) during Ramadan. The holiday is known under various other names in different languages and countries around the world.

cultural_events.name: Cocos Islands Day
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event celebrating the unique heritage and history of the islands.

wiki.extract: Cocos Island is a volcanic island in the Pacific Ocean administered by Costa Rica, approximately 550 km southwest of the Costa Rican mainland. It constitutes the 11th of the 15 districts of Puntarenas Canton of the Province of Puntarenas. With an area of approximately 23.85 km2 (9.21 sq mi), the island is roughly rectangular in shape. It is the southernmost point of geopolitical North America if non-continental islands are included, and the only landmass above water on the Cocos tectonic plate.

food_writeup: The cuisine of the Cocos (Keeling) Islands reflects a blend of Malay and Australian influences, featuring seafood, coconut-based dishes, and traditional Malay spices.
brief_history: Discovered in 1609, the islands were settled by the Clunies-Ross family in the 19th century who established a coconut plantation economy. The territory became an Australian external territory in 1955.

important_people.name: John Clunies-Ross

commentary.inflation_management: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands are an Australian external territory of around 600 people using the Australian dollar; no monetary policy and no IMF data exist. The cash economy is tiny - a small public sector, limited tourism, and copra's long decline - with most goods imported at high freight cost. Price levels simply follow Australian inflation plus remoteness premia.
commentary.debt_management: There is no sovereign borrowing; the islands are funded through the Australian federal budget. The strategic value of the territory (its Indian Ocean location and airfield) far exceeds its economic weight, and defence-related infrastructure spending is the main source of investment. Economic self-sufficiency is not a realistic prospect at this scale.

key_events.event: Continued Australian administration with gradual upgrades to the Cocos airfield's strategic role.
COVID-19 border closures isolated the islands, underscoring dependence on air links for supplies.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: The islands' significance is strategic, not economic: expect further Australian defence infrastructure investment given Indian Ocean competition. The civilian economy will remain a small, subsidized community. Climate and sea-level risk to the low atolls is the main long-term threat to habitability.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
